component.name: Vibemapp
component.summary: See your ZSA keyboard layout and switch layers per app

description.p: Vibemapp is a companion app for ZSA keyboards running Oryx firmware, such as the Voyager, Moonlander and ErgoDox EZ.

ul.li: Smart Layers: switch the keyboard to a layer automatically when you focus an app
Optional window title patterns for finer-grained rules
See every layer of your Oryx layout, following the keyboard live
Watch key presses as you type, with tooltips for every key
Optional key heatmap: see which keys you use most, per layer, app and period. Only per-key press counts are stored, never what you type
Optional typing insights: how your key presses are spread over your fingers and hands
Runs quietly in the tray or in the background

description.p: Smart Layers currently requires the Hyprland compositor.

screenshot.caption: Your Oryx layout with the active layer
Smart Layers switches layers per app
An opt-in heatmap of your key presses
Overlay settings: which layers show it, where and how large
Insights: the load on each finger and the hand split

description.p: The Insights screenshot now shows the page with Finger Load only.

The Insights page now shows Finger Load only: how your key presses are spread over your fingers and hands. Same-finger pairs, reach, layer switches, the score and the layout comparisons are gone, and key pairs are no longer recorded.
Layer change notifications can skip chosen layers, such as a mouse layer the keyboard turns on by itself, so moving between windows while using the trackpad no longer floods you with notifications.
The package now declares its dependency on python-cairo, which the overlay needs.
Smart Layers can show a desktop notification when it switches the layer, naming the layer and the app it switched for. It is off by default; turn it on in Preferences.

The heatmap can be filtered by app. A new Insights page scores your typing per finger and hand, shows same-finger pairs, reach and layer switches, and compares well-known layouts such as Colemak-DH against your current one. Key-pair counting is a separate opt-in and never stores what you type.
The overlay fades in and out again, with a Fade Duration setting on the Overlay page (200 ms by default, 0 for instant).

ul.li: Hiding the overlay no longer takes keyboard focus away from another app's panel, such as a session menu opened while holding a layer key
The overlay no longer briefly shows the previous layer when it appears

description.p: Smart Layers no longer undoes a layer you switched to by hand when the window title changes, for example when a terminal sets its title after every command. Switching to another app still applies its layer.
Smart Layers no longer switches layers while you hold keys, so a held layer key isn't dropped when focus moves to another window. The switch happens when you release the keys.

ul.li: A see-through, click-through overlay of the active layer that lights up the keys you press, shown on the layers you choose (needs gtk4-layer-shell)
The overlay has the same physical size on every monitor, can follow the focused monitor, and can spread the keyboard halves apart
Toggle the overlay from the tray or with vibemapp --toggle-overlay bound to a Hyprland key
The tray menu shows the keyboard and layer at the top, offers Show or Hide depending on the window, and has a Preferences entry
A stale setting left over from older versions is cleaned up automatically
Development builds run next to the installed app and warn when both control the keyboard
Transparent keys are now shown in the layout view, with the key they fall through to
Packaging no longer includes stale tray bytecode
Simpler Add Rule choices; All Steam Games uses the Steam icon
No more deprecation warnings when building the package
Smart Layers rule for all Steam games at once
Advanced rules that match window classes with a regular expression, with a live preview
Steam games are recognised by their Proton window class or by the game ID Steam gives native games
Hyprland autostart hint uses the Lua configuration syntax
The window always opens on the Layout page

description.p: KeyMapp for Linux is now called Vibemapp. Your settings and Smart Layers rules are carried over automatically.

ul.li: New Heatmap page: opt-in per-key press counts for today, the last 7 days or all time, per layer, with your most used keys
Tray icon: closing the window keeps Vibemapp in the tray, with quick access to Smart Layers and the current layer
Key tooltips now follow the pointer from key to key

description.p: First release, with Smart Layers for Hyprland and a live layout viewer.
